Important: This is a contract/part-time role: 10-20 hrs/week - rate $40-50/hr

NOPE is an AI safety company with a unique goal; we do not concern ourselves with bio or cyber-risks or other Hollywood-ized alignment fantasies. We are concerned instead with the massive proliferation of relationships between humans and AI and how this affects our wellbeing and societal fabrics. Billions of conversations between people and AI are accumulating into relationships. This ranges children talking to toys, adults with AI companions, or elderly people engaging with healthcare assistants. We measure real conversations and relationships, and the trajectories of risks involved, and publish what we find, so platforms (and society) can decide when and how to act. We build ML models, track incidents, analyze new regulations, and run evaluations constantly on both raw LLMs and deployed AI. We believe you cannot foster safe and aligned AI without proprer governance and scrutiny into AI as it is truly deployed and productized. The eval space in AI is currently heavily oriented to raw LLM evals unfortuntely. We seek to change that. We seek to hold AI labs and products to account for the harms they produce.
Our mission is malleable and always changing, and we search for people who seek to help define that.
The Social Comms role: We are doing quite a lot but are very limited on social-and-community-driving capacity. The incidents and regulations we track, the whitepapers, plus our evaluations, are all lacking our commentary and voice. We want to increase our social media presence significantly and start to be a more active participant in the global conversation around AI safety and alignment.
As our social-comms person you'd take artifacts and research we produce and weave them into a consistent, human presence on the prevalent social channels: deciding what gets posted, writing it, engaging with the researchers, journalists, builders and policymakers already wrestling with these questions. You're a pundit, optimist, skeptic, researcher and writer all rolled into one.Â 
The measure of your work would be whether the right people are actually engaging: researchers, builders, journalists, policymakers, and the ordinary users who sense something is off. No growth-hacking or engagement bait please. We would rather stay small and authoritative than sound like a brand. The work is async, any timezone, and you'd have direct access to the passionate team and to everything we publish before it's public.

You will have a significant say and authorship of our blog (nascent stages still), linkedin, other social accounts, public spaces, and private community spaces that you recommend. Anything relevant to our work.

You'd be a great fit if
• You care deeply about what AI is doing to human relationships and social norms; you're concerned and curious.
• You understand how LLMs work at an abstract level and the flaws they have.

• You've run or grown popular social accounts before.
• You write like a person, and you don't lean on AI to think or post for you.
• You can read a piece of research and find the three lines people will actually care about.
• You can disagree with strangers thoughtfully in public, critics included.
• You have a feel for which channels matter, and which ones aren't worth our time.
• You have experience in civic domains, public-good, policy, trust-and-safety, or non-profits.
Bonus: you have already published material relevant to AI and its proliferation and risks.

Please mention the word **AWARD** and tag RNzQuMjQ5Ljc5LjUx when applying to show you read the job post completely (#RNzQuMjQ5Ljc5LjUx). This is a beta feature to avoid spam applicants. Companies can search these words to find applicants that read this and see they're human.

f429e258084d4cec.description:
BOSS-IQ | CTO Partner | REMOTE (worldwide) | Full-time | Istanbul-based company | https://boss-iq.com
BOSS-IQ is an AI strategic-planning product for owner-operators of small and medium businesses. The boss describes an idea that has been stuck for years; a research-and-question session returns an implementation-ready plan. In production since June, hand-onboarding our first paying customers since August, invitation-only.
I am looking for a partner rather than a first hire, and I need two things in one person. An experienced developer who has genuinely run software in production — deployments, incidents, on-call. And a black-belt prompter. I mean that as a level, not a flourish. The tell: if you watch other developers work in AI environments and feel real frustration — everyone prompts, most prompt badly — and you have quietly built your own standing rule files, your own context discipline, your own reusable prompt library, then you already know what I am describing. That is the rarer of the two skills, and the one I weight hardest.
Under the product, 60+ specialist agents run continuous extraction over each customer's documents and sessions into a persistent, per-company memory: every fact dated and traced to its source sentence, contradictions kept rather than overwritten — a discipline we call Total Capture. Patent-pending since July, in context engineering.
Stack: TypeScript throughout. A NestJS API plus a separate NestJS worker on Railway, Next.js 16 / React 19 on Vercel, Postgres with Prisma, Redis and BullMQ, Pinecone, S3-compatible storage. Agents are LangChain.js / LangGraph ReAct agents on Anthropic Claude across three model tiers, with OpenAI embeddings. Every prompt body and model config lives in one versioned master file synced to LangSmith, never hardcoded in TypeScript.
I am the founder, and not an engineer — thirty years a strategy consultant, first terminal at the end of 2022. A contract developer built the first ~20,000 lines between December and February. Since February I have been the only developer, and it is now about 264,000 lines of TypeScript. I wrote the prompts first, 18,500 lines across 79 agent files, and the code came after to serve them.
That was the environment, not me: 45 interconnected instruction files deploying sub-agents, around 300,000 words of standing rules, orchestrated by one always-on kernel that classifies each session, auto-attaches the rules matching the files being touched, and generates sub-agentic plans for the work.
Compensation is the honest startup shape: generous equity, austerity salary. No number here — it is set against what you currently earn, and that is a conversation rather than a billboard.
Full posting: https://boss-iq.com/cto-partner.html
Apply: https://boss-iq.com/apply-cto.html — one question at a time, ending by asking you to write the prompts you would use on day one, not code. I read every one myself.
Or write to me directly: ahmet@boss-iq.com

About Sarvam
Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India. The company is developing India’s full-stack sovereign AI platform, building across research, models, infrastructure and applications with a singular focus on making AI genuinely work for India. Sarvam works with leading enterprises and public institutions and is backed by Lightspeed, Peak XV, and Khosla Ventures. Sarvam partners with India’s leading brands, including Tata Capital, SBI Life, CRED, IDFC, and LIC.
 
About the Role
DevRel at Sarvam is part engineering, part content, part community — and this role manages the community pillar.
You will be the person who makes Sarvam's developer community a place builders want to belong to. That means running our Discord day to day, designing and operating community programs — hackathons, meetups, office hours, workshops — and making sure every developer who shows up gets a great experience, whether they're asking their first question or shipping their tenth project.
But community at Sarvam isn't just events and engagement metrics. At the core of this role is empathy: you notice where developers get stuck, what they're excited about, and what's missing — and you carry that insight back to the engineering and product teams to close the loop. Feedback is not a side effect of this role. It's one of its most important outputs.
 
What You’ll Do
• 
Manage the Discord community — manage our developer community: moderation, onboarding flows, channel structure, engagement rituals, and maintaining channels by triaging questions and routing them to the right people.
• 
Design and run community programs — plan and execute hackathons, meetups, office hours, workshops, and campus outreach end to end: concept, logistics, promotion, on-the-ground execution, and follow-up.
• 
Recognise and grow our best builders — identify our most engaged developers and create structured ways to recognise them, give them a platform, and help them grow within the community.
• 
Grow the community — run initiatives that bring new developers in: partnerships with colleges and developer communities, collaborations with other devtool ecosystems, and community-led content.
• 
Be the voice of the community — synthesise what developers are saying into structured feedback for the engineering, product, and DevRel teams. Spot recurring friction points and champion fixes.
• 
Track what matters — monitor community health metrics (activity, retention, response times, program participation, NPS) and use them to decide what to double down on.
What We're Looking For
• 
1–3 years of experience in community management, developer programs, or a related role — ideally in a devtools, developer platform, or open-source ecosystem.
• 
You have experience building a community from the ground up — and scaling it. You've started something with a handful of members and grown it into a real, active community. You know what it takes at every stage, from the first ten people to the first ten thousand.
• 
You're comfortable around developers and code. You don't need to be an engineer, but you should understand how developers work, be able to follow technical conversations, and know when a question needs an engineer's answer.
• 
You're an organiser at heart. Events, logistics, follow-ups, timelines — you enjoy running things end to end and nothing falls through the cracks on your watch.
• 
You write clearly and warmly. Announcements, Discord replies, program docs — your writing makes people feel welcome and informed.
• 
You move fast and follow through. You can take a loosely defined brief — "run a hackathon next month" — and ship something polished without being hand-held.
• 
You're genuinely community-minded. You find energy in helping other builders succeed, and you treat every interaction as a chance to learn what the community needs.
• 
Bonus: You've organised hackathons or large meetups, run community programs at scale, have experience with community tooling (Discord bots, analytics), or have an interest in AI and Indian languages.
Why Sarvam?
Sarvam is a fast-moving, high talent-density team building full-stack AI for India, working on problems that push the frontiers of AI with real population-scale impact.
Work alongside researchers, engineers, builders, and business leaders who move fast and hold each other to a very high bar
High ownership and high impact, from day one
Everything we do is AI-first, from the way we build and ship to the way we think about problems
You can work on problems that could change how an entire country learns, works, and communicates
If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI in India, Sarvam is the place to be.
